latest_human_steering: Every subject-graph entity is an Entity, including Nodes, Properties and CFEL Relations. Entity is a generic Term, not a restored Entity root. No standalone wildcard is needed; inheritance is intended.

findings.evidence: CA-R-2462 explicitly scopes its MODEL default and HAS_PROPERTY allowance to (Node, Node.**), and instance permissions to Node instance and its dependent Properties. CA-R-2471 says Node.** selects recursive dependents of Node; Node rules inherit into applicable narrower Nodes. CA-R-2278 says narrower declarations inherit applicable broader constraints; containment does not add inheritance.
findings.consequence: These pins establish the Node branch, not that Relation, Operator, Carrier or Term inherit Node.

findings.evidence: CA-R-2247 defines Relation under CFEL; CA-R-2616 defines CFEL Operator; CA-R-1958 defines Carrier; CA-R-1318 defines Term. CA-R-2355 explicitly declares Relation.Name and CA-R-2415 explicitly declares Term.Name. CA-R-2471 says X.p addresses a Property borne by X.
findings.consequence: Current model already discusses bearer-qualified non-Node properties. No matching Node-narrowing declaration for these bearer kinds was found in this bounded trace; do not infer that they inherit Node or that their Properties are identical to Node.**.

findings.evidence: CA-R-2473 defines IS_PROPERTY_OF from Property to any applicable declared model Entity or instance and HAS_PROPERTY as its derived inverse; CA-R-2621 declares the inverse. CA-R-2588 resolves default and named constraints by host, relation, target and layer and requires each inverse direction to have its own applicable named outgoing permission.
findings.consequence: The Relation definition supplies endpoint meaning, not automatic per-host inverse permission. No blanket wildcard prohibition was found for reviewed non-Node bearers; absence of an inspected non-Node whitelist is not evidence of prohibition or permission.

findings.evidence: CA-R-1259 states every Entity may bear zero or more Property occurrences and states a HAS_PROPERTY bound on Entity. CA-R-2462 provides the analogous named outgoing HAS_PROPERTY entry for the Node branch.
findings.consequence: The universal rule duplicates that allowance within the Node branch but states a broader all-Entity bearer capability that CA-R-2462 alone does not establish. Keep the user’s universal meaning; do not narrow or retire it as redundant solely from Node inheritance.

findings.evidence: CA-R-2462 has both `(Node, Node.**) {:0..1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF))` without a written target and `Node.** {:1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) (Node, Node.**)`; CA-R-2588 requires resolving target-domain applicability and treats omitted endpoint counts independently.
findings.consequence: The effect of the target-omitted named constraint on a Node.** Property targeting a non-Node bearer is not proved by this bounded trace. Do not assert such a link is forbidden or automatically permitted without resolving its applicable target domain.

minimal_disposition: Preserve R1259 universal meaning and do not add a new Entity root, wildcard, classification or fabricated permission. Reconcile how the existing generic Entity term governs universal bearer applicability and how target-omitted and explicit endpoint permissions interact; then choose the canonical existing Subject for R1259 without narrowing its Claim.
question_if_needed: Under the existing relation and inheritance rules, does R1259’s universal prose establish the per-Entity HAS_PROPERTY permission for non-Node bearers, and how does the target-omitted IS_PROPERTY_OF bound interact with the explicit Node-bearer signature?
limits: This is a bounded source trace, not an exhaustive model or runtime census.
